column130: Applied machine learning for predictive maintenance in industrial IoT systems, specifically the development of anomaly-detection algorithms for manufacturing equipment failure prediction.
column131: My work focuses on building machine learning models that analyze real-time sensor data from industrial equipment (vibration, temperature, and pressure readings) to predict mechanical failures before they occur. This sits at the intersection of applied machine learning, time-series analysis, and industrial systems engineering. Over the past four years, I have developed anomaly-detection pipelines using LSTM neural networks and gradient-boosted decision trees, applied specifically to reducing unplanned downtime in manufacturing environments.
column132: Traditional predictive maintenance relies on fixed-threshold sensor alerts, which generate high false-positive rates and fail to catch gradual degradation patterns. My approach combines a custom feature-engineering pipeline with an ensemble model architecture that reduced false-positive alerts by approximately 40% in pilot deployments at two manufacturing facilities. I hold one pending patent application (U.S. Application No. 17/XXX,XXX) for a novel sensor-fusion technique used in this model, and have published one peer-reviewed paper on the methodology at a 2023 IEEE industrial computing conference.
column133: Unplanned equipment downtime costs U.S. manufacturers an estimated $50 billion annually. By enabling more accurate failure prediction, my methodology has the potential to reduce maintenance costs and production losses across the manufacturing sector. In pilot implementations, the approach reduced unplanned downtime by 25% at partner facilities, translating to estimated annual savings of $2–3 million per facility. Broader adoption of this approach could meaningfully improve efficiency and competitiveness in U.S. advanced manufacturing, a sector the Department of Labor has identified as a national economic priority.
column134: Unplanned industrial equipment failure is a significant driver of productivity loss across the U.S. manufacturing sector, which the Department of Commerce has identified as critical to national economic competitiveness and supply chain resilience. My research on predictive maintenance directly supports the goals outlined in federal advanced manufacturing initiatives, including efforts to reduce reliance on foreign manufacturing by improving the efficiency and reliability of domestic production. The methodology I have developed is applicable across multiple manufacturing sub-sectors (automotive, semiconductor, and heavy machinery), giving it broad relevance beyond any single employer or industry segment.
column135: I hold a Master's degree in Computer Science from San Jose State University with a specialization in machine learning, and I have four years of hands-on experience building and deploying predictive maintenance models in live industrial environments. I have a pending U.S. patent application related to my sensor-fusion methodology and a peer-reviewed publication at a 2023 IEEE conference. My current role at TechNova Solutions Inc. gives me continued access to real-world industrial datasets and manufacturing partners needed to further develop and validate this work, and I maintain ongoing collaboration with two manufacturing facilities that have piloted my models in production.
column136: Broader adoption of my predictive maintenance methodology would reduce unplanned downtime costs for U.S. manufacturers, estimated at $50 billion annually nationwide, while improving the reliability of domestic production capacity. This supports national interests in reshoring manufacturing and strengthening supply chain resilience. Additionally, as an open contributor to the applied ML research community, my published methodology allows other U.S.-based engineers and companies to build on this work, creating a multiplier effect on the sector rather than benefiting a single employer alone
column137: Over the next two years, I plan to: (1) expand my current sensor-fusion model to additional equipment types beyond vibration/temperature sensors, including acoustic and electrical signature analysis; (2) finalize and file for full patent protection on the underlying methodology (currently at provisional patent stage); (3) publish two additional peer-reviewed papers documenting results from expanded pilot deployments; and (4) partner with at least one additional U.S. manufacturing facility to validate the approach at larger scale. To date, I have completed successful pilot deployments at two facilities, reducing unplanned downtime by 25%, and have a provisional patent application on file (as referenced in Section 2).
